images.scene: A majestic vintage merchant sailing ship gliding on a perfectly calm, glassy sea, seen from the side. The dark hull is LARGE in the frame, filling the bottom half and bleeding off the bottom edge. Along the waterline, subtle clusters of barnacles and mussels crust the hull plates, and two or three SMALL, almost innocent-looking holes pierce the wood just above the waterline, quiet and easy to miss, no drama, no sinking, the ship perfectly serene and proud. The masts and sails dissolve upward into bright pale haze.

A busy prosperous 1950s harbor quay: stevedores carrying sacks and wooden crates up a gangplank onto a moored cargo ship, a dockside crane lifting a loaded net, stacked goods everywhere, thriving trade in motion. The workers and cargo fill the bottom half of the frame, bleeding off the bottom edge. The space above them is bright, pale, hazy and empty.

The dark wooden hold of an old cargo ship: a single THIN trickle of water seeping through a seam between two hull planks, catching the dim glow of a hanging oil lantern, a small puddle barely forming on the floor, stacked dry crates nearby, quiet and almost invisible. The hull planks and trickle fill the bottom half of the frame, bleeding off the bottom edge. The space above is bright, pale, hazy and empty.

The same dark wooden ship hold much later: still water flooding the floor and rising halfway up the stacked wooden crates, soaked burlap sacks, gentle reflections on the water surface, a shaft of pale light falling from an open hatch above, no people. The flooded cargo fills the bottom half of the frame, bleeding off the bottom edge. The space above is bright, pale, hazy and empty.
